title: Alchemical Symbols

slides.text: Gold was the Sun. Lead was Saturn.
Gold: Sun. Silver: Moon. Iron: Mars. Copper: Venus. Tin: Jupiter. Lead: Saturn. Quicksilver: Mercury. One glyph served both.

slides.text: Fire rises: a triangle pointing up. Water sinks: a triangle pointing down. Bar them through, and they become air and earth.

slides.text: The Arabic Jabirian writings taught that metals were born of sulphur and mercury. In the 1500s, Paracelsus added a third principle: salt.

image.title: Aureolus Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim [Paracelsus]. Woodcut by A. Hirschvogel, 1538.
image.credit: Aureolus Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim [Paracelsus]. Woodcut by A. Hirschvogel, 1538. — Wellcome Collection (public domain)

slides.text: John Dee's Monas Hieroglyphica fused Moon, Sun, cross and the sign of Aries into one glyph. He claimed it held the cosmos.

image.title: Monas hieroglyphica / [John Dee].
image.credit: Monas hieroglyphica / [John Dee]. — Wellcome Collection (public domain)

slides.text: Carl Jung's Psychology and Alchemy read these glyphs as maps of the unconscious. Principe and Newman later restored the laboratory behind them.

image.title: Sigmund Freud, Stanley Hall, Carl Gustav Jung, Abraham Arden Brill, Ernest Jones and Sándor Ferenczi. Photograph, 1909.
image.credit: Sigmund Freud, Stanley Hall, Carl Gustav Jung, Abraham Arden Brill, Ernest Jones and Sándor Ferenczi. Photograph, 1909. — Wellcome Collection (public domain)

slides.text: Carl Linnaeus took the glyphs of Mars and Venus, iron and copper, to mark male and female. They never left.

image.title: Carolus Linnaeus. Line engraving after G. Lundberg, 1751.
image.credit: Carolus Linnaeus. Line engraving after G. Lundberg, 1751. — Wellcome Collection (public domain)

slides.text: Which glyph would you carve into your door: Saturn's lead, Mercury's quicksilver, or the Sun's gold? Tell us why.

caption:
Before the periodic table, there was a cipher.

Seven metals. Seven planets.
Four triangles for the elements.
Three principles: sulphur, mercury, salt.

The alchemists did not write plainly.
They wrote in sigils meant to conceal the work from the unworthy.

A green lion eating the sun.
A monad said to hold the universe.
A notation Jung mistook for the soul and Principe proved was also chemistry.

Some of these signs still sit in every biology textbook.
Most readers never notice.

Section 11 decodes the full sign system: planetary glyphs, elemental marks, the operations, and the scholars who cracked them.

The full entry waits in the Forbidden Library: alloccult.com/symbols-sigils/alchemical-symbols

review_log.summary: Accurate, on-brand carousel with nothing blocking. Facts check out: the planet-metal pairs, the elemental triangles, Jabirian sulphur-mercury theory and Paracelsus' salt, Dee's Monas (Antwerp 1564), Jung's Psychology and Alchemy (Zurich 1944) and Linnaeus' first use of the sex symbols (1751). Optional polish: slide 2's saltpetre-workshop image is only loosely related, slide 6 should give Principe and Newman's first names, and the caption overstates the Jung/Principe contrast and cites an opaque 'Section 11'.
